turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How can I help you today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Hi um, I'm bringing my one year old daughter in because she's had this fever um, this runny nose and this cough, for the past three, four days. Um, and now, she sounds pretty wheezy.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and um, as she had a fever the entire time over the past three or four days.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I would say so like it's come and gone, but every time I checked her temperature, I tried to check her twice a day, it would be pretty high, like 38 or uh, 39.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, so it was between 38 and 39 each time you checked it.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, and now I should mention like um, I checked today and she didn't have a fever today, but she sounds really wheezy now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, is the wheeze new today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, and the cough, that started about three or four days ago as well?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, that's right.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how, how does the cough sound? Does it sound like, barky or like a, seal-like cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, it sounds pretty harsh. I don't know if it sounds barky.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and is the cough worse at any particular time of the day, like morning or night?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no it's, it's just always there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, uh, is she bringing up any, any phlegm or sputum?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, she's bringing up some, um, she's, she actually, she used to bring up some phlegm, but now it's, it's pretty dry.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, so she was bringing up phlegm initially and is no longer. What colour was it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It was clear.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, any blood that you noticed there?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, no blood.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, and yeah, she's, she's had a wheeze as well. Um, have you noticed, uh, any chest pain, if she's like pointing to her chest or anything?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and has she had any, any like fainting spells?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Um, and, yeah so she's had a fever, has she had any like, chills or night sweats, like where she's shaking?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh no, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how has her mood been?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: She's been pretty fussy, um, yeah, she's been pretty fussy over the past few days, but I just thought it was because of how she was feeling um, like her symptoms.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, certainly. Has she been eating and drinking okay?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, we've managed to get her to drink and eat okay. Um, so, in that sense, no changes there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, how many diapers is she, how many wet diapers per day?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, about five.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, so yeah, still been to maintain hydration, it sounds like. Um, yeah, okay, and has she had any like, eye redness or eye discharge?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any suggestion that she might have um, like any ear pain or, or any ear discharge?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and has she had a runny nose?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um yeah, now that you mention it, yeah, she did have a runny nose. Um, it seems to be less now, but she did have a lot a few days ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and did that start around the same time as the cough and, and fever?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, it's still going on, but, but just less.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: That's right, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. On feeds or anything like that, did you notice like any redness in her, in the back of her throat?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I noticed some, um, yeah, I noticed some redness, but I just thought it was because of her coughing a lot.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, and um, have you noticed any skin changes or, or rashes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and any changes to bowel habits like diarrhea?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, no changes there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Then any changes to um, like urinary habits as well?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, no changes there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and have you noticed any like bulging on her, on her forehead or on the anterior fontanelle?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Um, and uh, has she had any nausea or vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not that I've noticed.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright. Um just yeah, she's been a little bit more, um, irritable as well. Um, okay, and has she had any symptoms like this before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I mean, when she was a few months old she had similar symptoms, um, and she was like hospitalized for maybe a day or two, but she became better.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, did she need like antibiotics or inhalers or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think they just gave her some oxygen and then um, some fluids.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Um, has she been diagnosed with any medical conditions before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and besides that one time going, like going to the hospital, has she been hospitalized or had any surgeries?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, before that she was fine.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, uh, are the immunizations up to date?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, everything's up to date.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Excellent. Um, and in terms of the pregnancy itself, were there any complications throughout um, with mom?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, no, no complications.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And was it a full term delivery, and vaginal or c-section?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It was uh, full time and it was vaginal.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, any concerns at birth, like jaundice or, or any types of distress?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how is her growth and development been thus far? Any concerns?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, that's great, and in terms of um, the home environment, who's living with her and um, who's primarily looking after her?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, so it's her dad and I, as well as her um, her grandma.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and has anybody in the home been sick recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, everyone's been healthy.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, and has there been any travel?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um no, we haven't gone anywhere recently.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, and does anybody uh, in the house smoke?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, and are there, are there any pets or are there any like carpets or um, linens that can hold, hold a lot of dust or dander?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, any other exposures, to like triggers, or potentially things that, that could be exposed or stuff like, that could be inhaled?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't have anything like that at home. It's a fairly new home and uh, it's hardwood floors, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Um, and uh, any family history of lung problems or heart problems?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, how about a family history of any congenital diseases or um, any genetic diseases?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, and family history of any cancer?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Um, so were there any other um, so that was everything that I wanted to ask today before I went on to the physical exam. Um, was there anything else that you, that you wanted to add or were wondering about that I maybe forgot to ask?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah um, what, what can we do for her um, to make her better? And are you concerned about her breathing?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um, so the, the physical exam and the, the vital signs will really, will help with um, to assess her breathing and to see oxygen levels.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um, and um, this could be uh, caused by um, a viral infection, which could be something along the lines of uh, like a common cold type picture, and we can get like inflammation of uh, really small airways, um, and it can cause that cough, and fever, and some of the symptoms that she's experiencing. And also, um, these symptoms do overlap with COVID as well, um, and so it'll be important to get a COVID swab just in case. Um, but um, if that is the, the scenario, then it will be um, supportive care with oxygen, fluids and we'll make sure that um, that her, her breathing is uh, okay. And possibly, we'll need steroids and um, and uh, an inhaler if necessary.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay. Okay, that sounds good, thank you.
